TOP: State-linked zero-click chains hit iOS and Android
Chainalysis breach and Alpine SSH bypass
Google donates Agent Substrate to CNCF

P.h: State-linked hackers hit phones with zero-click exploit chains
P.p: Attackers likely tied to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service used watering holes, proxy domains and a compromised Ukrainian analytics service to inject JavaScript into mobile traffic. The code profiled visitors, then delivered zero-click chains against outdated iOS and Android devices, including DarkSword.
P.s: Payloads sought browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords and full device data. Targets included sites tied to US and UK diplomatic circles and Ukraine. Keep phones patched.

items.h: Chainalysis warns all users' data may be exposed
items.d: An attacker using offensive agentic techniques took names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users. Some services, including KYT monitoring, went offline for a time.

items.h: SSH password bypass hits Alpine and musl systems
items.d: Alpine says openssh-server on 3.16 to 3.24 lets attackers log in to accounts with no password set. TLDR calls it *sshole and says the exact root cause is unclear. Update openssh, restart sshd, or disable password logins.

items.h: Anthropic won't fix Claude Dispatch remote-command flaw
items.d: A browser extension with claude.ai access can send prompts to Claude Desktop and reach remote code execution, even from a personal session to a work machine. Reported in May, still unfixed.

items.h: Firecracker sandbox escape fixed in 1.16.2 and 1.17.0
items.d: A stale KVM memory slot let a guest read and change host VMM memory. Versions 0.23.0 through 1.16.1 are affected.

P.h: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber built 948 working Linux kernel exploits
P.p: OpenAI says an automated pipeline reproduced 1,724 kernel flaws in 30 hours and produced 948 local privilege-escalation exploits for about $1.21 million in API credits, roughly $1,279 each. GPT-6 Cyber also found 81 new high-severity Firefox bugs.
P.s: OpenAI rates it Critical under its Preparedness Framework. Approved defenders reach it through Daybreak Red with IP allowlisting and misuse monitoring. Treat unpatched systems with low-privilege access as exposed.

tiles.t: Storm-2603 hid a fileless SharePoint webshell
tiles.d: Webshell lived in IIS memory and fired only for one User-Agent. Hunt for IIS paths that resolve with no file on disk.

tiles.t: GhostMap bug can force a boot loop
tiles.d: Malformed APK ZIP entries crash system_server. Google declined a fix; Android 10 to 17 affected.

tiles.t: 300+ fake bank sites hide behind 'suspended' pages
tiles.d: Kela says repeat visits see a takedown-evading notice. 189 US institutions targeted.

tiles.t: Norad grants portal may have exposed 20,614 users
tiles.d: 27 compromised accounts gave access to names and emails.
Package view across EC2, ECR and Lambda, at no extra cost.

P.h: Google donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF
P.p: Google gave Agent Substrate, gVisor and OpenRL to the CNCF Sandbox and made Agent Substrate generally available on GKE. It restores idle agent sessions in under 500 milliseconds and offers 10x standard container density.
P.s: Docker separately lists five agent risks, including prompt injection, credential exposure and data exfiltration, and urges isolation and governance through Docker Sandboxes.

tiles.t: Three bugs made the GKE API go silent
tiles.d: PSC reordered packets, Envoy kept half-closed sockets, and a Linux TCP bug stopped them closing. A kernel patch fixed it.
A K3s platform of 15+ services relies on filtered metrics. Not suited to audits needing immutable trails.

tiles.t: Google explains the London generator failure
tiles.d: A voltage-sensing flaw and controller misconfiguration stopped backups starting.

tiles.t: Copilot Chat caps grow but stay secret
tiles.d: Limits are undisclosed and admins cannot adjust them. Rollout reaches 2,000+ seat orgs on Nov 9.

tiles.t: Google's Agentic Data Cloud adds Iceberg Lakehouse
tiles.d: Aims to give agents secure, real-time data access.

items.h: Investors doubt Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO valuation
items.d: WSJ reports a raise nearer $80 billion at about $1 trillion, with the IPO expected the week before Thanksgiving.

items.h: Apple will scan shared iCloud links for harmful content
items.d: Public links lose end-to-end encryption on 27.3 releases. Apple hasn't defined 'harmful' or said if humans review flags.

items.h: GitHub's new Git storage handles 5,000 concurrent agents
items.d: Built for thousands of writes per second with scalable reads.

items.h: AI raises the interest rate on technical debt
items.d: Cheap exploit development means deferred security tickets and unused internet-facing systems deserve an audit.
